day: My knees say rain. My knees are never wrong, only early.
A lamp is just a promise you keep every evening.
evening: Look at that. Dusk, and not one lamp lit. I used to do forty before supper.
Mind the dark, traveller. It is not empty.
night: Nobody should be about. Go home. Or go in. Or at least go lit.

topics.label: The Lamps
topics.text: Every road in Hollowmere had a lamp every forty paces once. The Lamplighters kept them. I was the last. When my knees went, the dark came back a step at a time.

topics.label: The Hollow
topics.text: The Hollow is the old hall in the middle of the meadows. It has a lamp - the Great Lamp - that lit the whole country. It went out the night the debts came due.

topics.label: Your debt
topics.text: I borrowed light from a place that does not forget. That is all I will say before the ledger is found.

day: Rooms are 10 pennies. The stew is free if you tell me something I have not heard.
Mind the boots. Mind the cat. Mind the cat's boots.
evening: Busy night coming. Sit anywhere that is not mine.
night: Quiet, quiet. The ale sleeps late, and so do I.

topics.label: Rumours
topics.text: Wolves have been bold along the north trail. The Rook gang has set up in the old woodcutters' camp east of the Greywood, and a bridge fell in the Kestrel River last spring - nobody has mended it.

topics.label: A bed
topics.text: Press B on any bed to rest. At the inn it costs ten pennies; it skips to morning and heals you fully.

day: Welcome! Everything has a price and most of it is fair.
Bring me flax, mushrooms, anything you find. I do not ask where.
evening: Closing soon. Last chance for tapers.
night: Shop is shut. Knock at dawn.

topics.label: Selling
topics.text: I buy what you gather: herbs, ore, pelts, odds and ends. Open the shop and switch to Sell.

day: If it can be hit, I can improve it.
Forge is hot. The forge is always hot.
evening: Ale first. Iron after.

topics.label: Smithing
topics.text: Smelt ore into ingots at any forge. Ingots become swords and coats. A skilled hand makes better steel - practise.

day: Cuts, coughs, curses - I treat two of the three.
Drink water. Walk it off. Do not touch the red mushrooms.
evening: Evening patients are the interesting ones.

topics.label: Herbs
topics.text: Heather and reedmint make a good tonic. Linen makes bandages. Fever needs reedmint and a berry or two.

day: Steady. The roads are wilder than they were.
Keep your blade clean and your lamp lit.
evening: Curfew soon. Wolves get hungry at dusk.
night: Go indoors, if you have any sense.

topics.label: The Rooks
topics.text: Captain Rook's gang squats in a palisade camp in the east woods, past Tidewick's road. They come to the roads at night. Whoever ends them will be paid from the watch purse.

day: I counted the lamps! There are lots! And some that are not!
Are you a hero? You look a bit tired for a hero.
evening: I am not afraid of the dark. The dark is afraid of Marrow.
night: Shh. I am supposed to be asleep.

topics.label: The cave
topics.text: There is a cave in the Greywood with roots like doors. I saw it from the cart road. It breathes. Do not tell Mum I told you.

day: Tidewick takes what the sea gives and gives back what it can spare.
If a ship comes in, it is on my ledger. If it does not, it is on my conscience.
evening: Tide is turning. Mind the pier.
night: The pier is slick after dark. Do not fall in; I will not fish you out.

topics.label: Kestrel Bridge
topics.text: The Kestrel Bridge is the quickest road between the meadows and the moor. It fell in spring. Brisk the carpenter can rebuild it if someone brings planks and iron.

day: Rope, oil, tapers, pearls. All honest. Mostly.
Caravans of light came in by the beacon, they say. I had a lens the size of my fist.
evening: Closing. Come back when the gulls do.
night: Closed. The gulls are asleep and so should you be.

topics.label: Pearls
topics.text: Salt pearls wash up on the Tidewick shallows. I buy them at a fair price - fair to me.

day: Measure twice. Cut once. Argue forever.
I could build you a bridge. I could build the whole country a bridge.
evening: Sawdust makes a man thirsty.

topics.label: The bridge
topics.text: Twelve planks and four ingots of iron. Bring them to me and I will have the Kestrel Bridge up in a day. That is a promise I can keep.

day: The Drowned Rat has never drowned a rat. We just like the name.
What will it be? The answer is ale.
evening: Sailors and liars; I serve both.
night: Last call is whenever I fall asleep.

topics.label: Rumours
topics.text: A hermit lives in the reeds near Reedholm. Says he saw a church sink. Says the bell still rings under the water on foggy nights. Nobody has checked.

day: The sea sends everything back eventually. Even people.
Hold this line. No - this one. Thank you.
evening: Dark soon. The gulls get nervous.

topics.label: Salt
topics.text: Some nights the beach glitters in the wrong colours. Star salt, the old women call it. It does not come from our sea.

day: Ore. I need ore. The moor gives it and the moor takes it back.
A sword is only as honest as its smith.
evening: Cooling the forge. Warming the throat.

topics.label: Ore
topics.text: Rust-red veins show on the moor between the boulders. Mine them with your sword hand - it is slow work - and bring the ore here.

day: The stones remember what the people forget.
Somebody keeps leaving coins on the Cairn of Debts. It frightens me. It should frighten you.
evening: The wind is getting a voice.

topics.label: The Cairn of Debts
topics.text: The Cairn is where Hollowmere buried its unpaid favours. It is not a grave. It is a ledger. The Collector keeps it still.

topics.label: The Stones
topics.text: On the high moor stand stones that sing when the sky does. If something out there has called, the stones will open for you.

day: Heather ale. It is exactly as bad as it sounds and twice as good.
Pull up a stool, stranger.
evening: Songs start at dusk.

topics.label: Rumours
topics.text: Moor folk say there is a cache walled up in the cliffs near the old stones. You have to knock the right chime to open it. I never learned the tune.

day: The sheep know more than I do and say less.
Wolves in the grey woods, hawks on the moor. Take both seriously.
evening: Counting. Counting.

topics.label: Wolves
topics.text: The wolf dens sit in the Greywood. Kill a few and the packs disperse for a season - that is all anyone can do.

day: The marsh breeds fevers as the meadow breeds wheat.
Rest. Rest. Do not argue.
evening: Lanterns are lit. Good. Good.

topics.label: Fever
topics.text: A fever is spreading through the stilt-houses. I need reedmint - the grey-green herb along the water. Six sprigs would be a mercy.

day: Everything in the marsh is for sale, including the marsh.
Mind the planks. Mind the mud. Mind your purse.
evening: Closing the shutters. Mosquitoes come with the lamps.

topics.label: The Chapel
topics.text: There is a chapel sunk in the Sallow, half under the water. There is a crypt below it and a bell. The bell is worth a fortune, or a funeral.

day: Lamp oil. The reason the country can see itself at night.
Slow work, oil. Like grief.
evening: Every lamp I press is a day I get to keep.

topics.label: Lamp oil
topics.text: The Great Lamp needs three flasks of my oil, and a coal that has never gone out. I can supply the oil.

day: The fields never rest. Neither do I.
If you are hungry, there is bread. If you are hungry and honest, there is stew.
evening: Lamp is lit. Come in or go on.

topics.label: The harvest
topics.text: Flax and berries, my rows are thin this year. If you are walking the meadows, think of me.

day: The reeds say things. The reeds do not lie. The reeds do not stop talking either.
I saw the chapel sink. I have been counting the bubbles since.
evening: It rings tonight. You can hear it if you stand still.
night: Keep your light low. They look up.

topics.label: The bell
topics.text: The Bell Warden took the chapel bell down with him. If someone rang it above water, the drowned could rest. I would pay in all I own, which is one boat.
